full_judgment: By this Rule the defendants opposite parties were called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 16.6.92 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 355 of 1969 dismissing the same should not be set aside. 2. The short facts giving rise to this Rule are, that the plaintiff petitioner filed the said suit for ejectment of the defendants opposite parties on the ground that Sirajuddin Mollah, the predecessor of the said opposite parties, was, monthly tenant under them and he became defaulter and violated the terms of tenancy agreement. The case of the petitioners is that they purchased the suit lands along with other lands and building from Rashik Lal Dey, one of the co-sharers of the property belonging to a partnership firm known as Laxmi Bhandar, by a registered deed dated 23.5.63. The original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah became a tenant under them who by admitting the petitioners as the title holder and his landlords executed tenancy agreement and paid rent by obtaining rent receipt after putting his thumb impression on the counterfoil of the same from the month of Falgoon 1368 BS to Jaistha 1370 BS at the previous rate fixed by the vendor of the petitioners. After some time the said defendant tenant stopped paying rent and filed a Title Suit No. 105 of 1968 and obtained an order of injunction and against the said order of temporary injunction the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 100 of 1968 and the appellate Court came to the finding that the petitioners acquired a right in the suit property and directed the defendant to pay rent to the petitioners. The further case of the plaintiffs petitioners was that the story of defendant's purchase of the suit land from one Shorat Babu and his brother Surendra Nath Biswas by a kabala dated 8.6.70 is false and collusive. The defendant now being defaulter tenants are liable to be ejected and hence the suit. 3. The original defendant No. 1 Sirajuddin Mollah, died after filing the written statement and thereafter his substituted heirs and the minors who are being represented by the court's guardian contested the suit by filing separate written statements-and denied the allegations of the plaint. Their main contention was that their predecessor Sirajuddin Mollah was never a tenant under the plaintiffs and it was also denied that their predecessor did not obtain any rent receipts by putting his LTI on the said counter for. It was further contended that the original defendant Sirajuddin filed Title Suit No.105 of 1968 against the plaintiff petitioners and obtained a temporary injunction and the plaintiffs petitioners preferred a Miscellaneous appeal against the said order of injunction and the said appeal was dismissed. It was further contended that the suit property along with other lands belonged to a joint business firm known as Laxmi Bhandar. About 40/50 years back the said original defendant was inducted as tenant in the suit property by the person in charge of the said property. Thereafter Nalini Kanti Biswas, son of Ashutush Biswas, having acquired the suit property measuring 18-1/2 decimals by way of amicable partition amongst his brother and other co-sharers by a kabala dated 27.7.69 and delivered possession to him and since then the defendants acquired title. It was further contended that one Abdul Majid Advocate was appointed a receiver in connection with different suits as between the share holder of the said firm named Laxmi Bhandar. The said Abdul Mojid used to realise the house rent from the said predecessor of the defendants. It was alleged that the husband of the plaintiff No. 1 in collusion with the said Abdul Mojid might have fabricated the papers by obtaining the impression of Sirajuddin taking advantage of his being an illiterate and simple person. The alleged thumb impression might have been taken by deceitful means and for which the said opposite parties are not bound by it. It was contended that the movable and immovable properties by Laxmi Bhandar were not partitioned by metes and bounds at any time and, as such, one of the share holders of the said business firm named Santosh Kumar Howlader filed partition suit No. 38 of 1972 at Khulna which is still pending. The defendants are possessing some portion of the suit land by themselves and other portion was let out to tenants and thereby they possessed the entire suit property as owners and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 4. The learned Assistant Judge upon hearing the parties dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree as aforesaid. The petitioners, being aggrieved thereby, moved this court under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act and obtained this Rule. 5. Mr. MA Rahim, the learned Advocate, appears for the petitioners and the learned Advocate Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder appears for the opposite parties. 6. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that Sirajuddin Mollah, the predecessor of the defendants opposite parties, was a monthly tenant of the suit land and the building under the petitioners by executing the unregistered deed of monthly tenancy agreement (Bhara Nama) Ext. 2 dated 1st. Ashar 1370 BS and on payment of rent by Ext. 1 the counterfoil of the rent receipt. In order to prove the said tenancy, the LTI of Late Sirajuddin appearing in those documents were compared by the hand writing expert who found those LTI tallied with specimen LTI obtained for the proof in the said title suit No. 41 of 1972 as renumbered from the said original Title suit No.105 of 1968 filed by the said original defendant against the petitioners for temporary injunction. In view of proof of tenancy of said Sirajuddin, the present defendants opposite parties are estopped from denying the monthly tenancy of Sirajuddin under the provisions of section 116 of the Evidence Act, the learned Assistant Judge having not applied his judicial mind in to considering that the plaintiffs petitioners proved the tenancy of the said original defendants, committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 7. Secondly, it has been submitted by Mr. Rahim that once a tenant is always a tenant and tenancy being heritable the defendants opposite parties are also the tenants under the plaintiffs since the plaintiffs acquired their title in the suit property by virtue of the registered kabala of 1963 and the admission said Sirajuddin being a tenant under the plaintiffs as proved by the recital of Bharanama Ext. 2 is binding upon the defendant opposite parties, as such, the learned court below committed error of law in not considering the said Ext. 2 in its proper perspective which has resulted in an error in decision causing failure of justice. 8. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the plaintiffs' kabala is of 1963 and the defendants' kabala is of dated 27.7.69 in respect of the same property clearly shows that the defendant till before their kabala of 1969 for about 6 years did not deny nor challenge the plaintiffs' right and title as landlord of the suit premises and they created kabala after the institution of the suit on 22.5.69 and the defendants' kabala being of a later date is hit by the doctrine of lis pendens under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act and the learned Assistant Judge committed error of law in not holding that the plaintiffs had prima facie title in view of the evidence on record and admission of the original defendant that the plaintiffs were his landlord and this has resulted in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 9. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has further submitted that the heirs of the original tenant Sirajuddin are estopped from setting up an independent title by the alleged subsequent purchase of the suit property after the filing of the plaintiffs' suit and the learned Assistant Judge thus failed to consider that suit for determination of tenancy was filed two months before the alleged title of the defendants in respect to the suit land and, as such, the plaintiffs were not obliged to file a suit for declaration of their title and recovery of possession and it is good enough for them to file a mere suit for establishment of tenancy right of said Sirajuddin, the predecessor of the defendants opposite parties at that time and, as such, the learned Assistant Judge failed to consider the aspect of the matter and thereby committed error of law in finding that the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable, is wrong and the same cannot be sustained in law. It has been further submitted by Mr. Rahim that the learned court below has travelled beyond the scope of the instant suit and unnecessarily embarked upon investigation on the question of title of the defendant without confining himself to the issue as to whether the plaintiff has been able to establish the tenancy of the defendants in the suit property. 10. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants opposite parties, on the other hand, contended that the predecessor of the defendants was never a tenant under the petitioners and both the parties claim the self same property by registered kabalas and in such view of the matter plaintiffs' suit for ejectment of the tenant without a suit for declaration of title is not maintainable and the learned court below rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree upon proper consideration of materials on record. It has been further submitted by Mr. Majumder that the alleged execution of Ext.2 (Bharanama) by Sirajuddin and the thumb impressions appearing therein and in the alleged counterfoil of the rent receipt are fabricated and those were obtained by fraudulent means and, as such the defendants are not bound by the recital of the said Ext. 2. Mr. Majumder has further submitted that the original defendant Sirajuddin Molla denied his being a monthly tenant under the plaintiffs and alleged that a fraud has been practised in the matter of obtaining his left hand thumb impressions in the said Exts. 1 and 2 and thereafter filed Title Suit No. 105 of 1968 against the plaintiffs and obtained an order of injunction and the said suit being re-numbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1972 is still pending and, as such, the present opposite parties cannot be estopped from asserting their own right and title in the suit property and the learned Assistant Judge has rightly observed that there exists a doubt regarding the validity of the said documents Exts. 1 and 2. 11. From the above submissions of the learned Advocates of the parties the points that call for determination in this case is whether the original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah was a tenant under the plaintiffs and secondly, whether the plaintiffs' suit as framed is maintainable. 12. I have heard the learned Advocates at length and perused the records. The whole argument of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties was that once a tenancy is denied by a tenant claiming an independent title in the self same property, the petitioners ought to have filed a full fledged suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. Repelling the above contention, Mr. Rahim has rightly argued that parties' right is to be determined at a time when the suit is instituted or when a course of action arises. In elaborating this point Mr. Rahim has pointed out that the plaintiffs' claim in suit property by way of purchase on 29.3.63 and the original defendant who was already in the suit land as tenant of the ex-owner, executed a tenancy agreement Ext. 2 with the petitioners on and from 1st Ashar 1370 BS that is, from the year 1963, and he also paid rent for some time admitting the petitioners (plaintiffs) as his landlord. The fact remains that the original defendants had no title whatsoever at that time. 13. It appears from the record that plaintiff-petitioners purchased the suit land from one Rashik Lal who was one of the co-sharers of the property belonging to a partnership firm named Laxmi Bhandar. The plaintiffs claim that original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah was their tenant but subsequently the payment of rent to them and then the dispute arose between the plaintiffs and the original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah who denied the right and title of the plaintiff petitioners. The said Sirajuddin Mollah brought a Title Suit No.105 of 1968 denying the right, title of the plaintiffs and prayed for an order of injunction restraining the plaintiffs petitioners not to disturb their possession and the suit was heard and the learned court concerned granted injunction in favour of the original defendant Serajuddin Mollah. Against the said order of injunction the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal and though the appeal was dismissed the court directed the said defendants to pay rent to the plaintiffs. The said Title Suit No.105 of 1968 of the defendants was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1972 which is still pending. It further appears from the record that the plaintiffs in order to prove the tenancy of the original defendant Serajuddin Mollah, filed counterfoil of the rent receipt Ext. 1 and Bharanama Ext. 2 and also filed their documents of title Ext. 5 (Ka) and in that suit they prayed for proving the left hand thumb impression of Serajuddin Mollah appearing in the said exhibits 1 and 2 by hand writing expert and for that purpose Serajuddin Mollah gave some specimen thumb impressions in court. It appears from the report of the hand writing expert that he compared the specimen thumb impressions with his thumb impressions appearing in said exhibits 1 and 2. The hand writing expert found that the LTI in Exts. 1 and 2 tallied with the specimen thumb impressions of Serajuddin Mollah. It further appears that Serajuddin Mollah admitted the petitioners as his landlord and agreed to pay the enhanced rent of Taka 75.00 in consideration of the improvement made in the suit properties by the petitioners, Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder tried to argue that the defendants opposite parties denied the tenancy under the plaintiffs and alleged that the LTI in the said exhibits 1 and 2 have been taken by practising fraud as Serajuddin was illiterate and a man of simple nature. Be that as it may, the report of the hand writing expert was accepted without any objection and was marked as Ext. 20. But the learned court below did not at all consider this aspect in the proper perspective and came to an abrupt finding to the affect that: “যদি ও আগুলাংক বিশারদ বাদী পক্ষে দাখিলী প্রদর্শন ১ ভাড়া আদায়ের রসিদ ও প্রদর্শন ২ অ- রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ভাড়ার চুক্তি পত্রে প্রদত্ত টিপ সহি সমূল মূল বিবাদী অধুনামৃত সিরাজ উদ্দিন মোল্লার বলিয়া পরীক্ষান্তে অভিমত ব্যক্ত করিয়াছেন, তথাপি উক্ত প্রদর্শন ১ ভাড়া আদায়ের রসিদের কাউন্টার ভাড়াটিয়ার স্বাক্ষরের স্থানসহ উহার উল্টা পিঠে, কোন রকম লিখন ব্যতীত শুধু মাত্র টিপসহি প্রদান এবং প্রদর্শন ২’২ অরেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ভাড়ার চুক্তি পত্রের নিচের দিকের একখানা টিপ সহি উপরের দিকে গৃহীতাদের নামের ঠিক উপরে অকারনে পরপর আরো ২ খানা বকলম বিহীন পিট, উক্ত ভাড়া রশিদ এবং চুক্তি পত্রের বৈধতা সম্পর্কে যথেষ্ট সন্দেহের সৃষ্টি করে।” 14. This finding is wrong because there are LTIs of Serajuddin Mollah in the said agreement Ext. 2 and in the counterfoil of rent receipt Ext.1 were tallied with the specimen thumb impressions for Sirajuddin Mollah and it was neither denied by him nor the report of the hand writing expert was challenged and, as such, the monthly tenancy of Serajuddin under the plaintiffs has been proved. When the tenancy of Serajuddin was prima facie found by the court of law in the earlier suit, the said tenant became defaulter then the plaintiffs petitioners filed the instant suit for his ejectment but the said defendant having died his legal heirs that is, the present defendants opposite parties, contested the instant suit and the learned court below failed to consider that the plaintiffs claim the suit land by purchase on 25.3.63 and suit was filed on 22.5.69 for ejectment of the tenants when there was no existence of the defendants' title in the self same suit property by way of purchase from a different co-sharer on 27.7.69. It shows that the plaintiffs' suit for determination of the tenancy was filed two months before the alleged title of the defendants and, in such circumstances, I am of the opinion that plaintiffs were not obliged to file a suit for declaration, rather the defendants who ought to have filed such suit for declaration by virtue of their subsequent title in the property, but they have not done so. Accordingly, I find that the suit for ejectment filed by the plaintiffs petitioners is quite maintainable in the above facts and circumstances of the case and accordingly, I find substance in the conception of Mr. Abdur Rahim that once a tenancy has been established the tenant must vacate first and then he can claim independent title. In this connection a reference may be made to a decision cited by Mr. Rahim in the case of Hajee Abdus Sattar vs. Mahiuddin and others reported in 6 BCR(AD) 71. I have gone through the said decision and the principle enunciated therein is applicable in the instant case as their Lordships held in the following language; "The estoppel as described in this Section is known as tenant's estoppel or estoppel by contract. This estoppel is founded upon a contract between the tenant and the landlord. It provides that when a person enters into possession of immovable property as a tenant of another person then neither he nor anybody claiming through him shall be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to deny the landlord's title, however defective that title might be. This necessarily implies that in case the tenant sets up a claim of title in himself he shall first surrender possession to the person from whom he had taken it." 15. On perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the court below disbelieved the story of tenancy virtually on suspicion without discussing the evidence on record in its proper perspective and came to the finding that the suit is not maintainable which is erroneous and cannot be sustained in law. 16. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate of the opposite parties, made a strong emphasis on the question that there are circumstances which proved that a fraud was practised upon the predecessor of the opposite parties in the matter of obtaining his thumb impression in the said Exts. 1 and 2, It is a settled principle of law that he who alleges fraud must prove it. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder could not place any material before me to find that any fraud has been practised by the petitioners in obtaining the LTI of said Serajuddin appearing in the said exhibits 1 and 2. I therefore, find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate as to the allegation of fraud and find that the said Ext. 1 and Ext. 2 are genuine documents to prove the tenancy of Serajuddin and that the same were legally proved by the plaintiffs and supported by the hand writing expert. In such view of the matter, there is no cogent reason to hold the said Serajuddin Mollah was not a tenant under the plaintiffs. Since tenancy is heritable and the present defendant opposite parties being the heirs of the said original tenant they are also deemed to be the tenants under the petitioners, 17. It appears from the record that there are various civil litigations including a partition suit between the alleged original co-sharers of the properties of the said business firm and ending in the court of law. It is not desirable for me to go into all those disputed questions of title. 18. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned court below, instead of confining itself to the question as to whether the plaintiffs have been able to prove the tenancy right of the original tenant defendant Serajuddin Mollah and whether the instant suit as framed is maintainable or not, unnecessarily embarked upon investigating and raising question of the defendants' title, and thereby misdirected itself in properly deciding the real issue in the suit and failed to apply his judicial mind. Accordingly I find it a legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree and the same is liable to be set aside. 19. In view of the above discussion I find that plaintiffs suit is maintainable in law. As the present defendants opposite parties stepped in to the shoes of the original tenant they arc also tenants under the petitioners until they could establish their independent title in the self same property by subsequent purchase. Since the present defendant opposite parties defaulted to pay the rent to the petitioners they are also defaulters and they are liable to be evicted. In view of the proposition of law as enunciated by the Appellate Division in the aforesaid decision, the opposite parties must surrender possession to the petitioners firstly and then they may seek remedy to establish their title in the property by subsequent purchase from a different co-owner, 20. For the reasons stated above I find merit in this revisional application. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned judgment and decree are set aside. However, there will be no order as to costs. End.
